documentation.rationale: The identity and terms half is strong: VIN, a Carfax bought by the buyer with a consistent odometer trail and clean brands, and a no-added-fees price. The maintenance half is nearly absent: two reported oil changes in 24 years, no age-related service, and no photos of the subframe, trunk floor or underbody.

condition.rationale: The exterior photos show straight, clean silver paint, a tidy soft top and wheels without obvious damage. Nothing proves the mechanical or structural condition. Long low-use corporate storage and 24 Michigan winters leave the cooling plastics, seals, tires and underbody unknown.

price_value.rationale: The $20,000 ask sits above the mileage-adjusted fair value of $13,840-$17,462 (mid $14,578). The car was bought at a fleet/lease auction on 08/25/2026 and relisted within two months with no documented reconditioning. Comparable low-mile peers ask $16-21k.

mission_fit.rationale: This is the target bridge car: a 2002 3.0i with a claimed manual, within the $27,000 ceiling, just above the ideal band, and easy to resell. Reliability is unproven because age-related service is undocumented after years of very low use.

logistics.rationale: The car is about 1,662 mi away in Burton, MI. The dealer ships nationwide and is responsive, but PPI access is not stated. CA registration needs a smog test. A fly-and-drive trip is feasible if a Michigan independent PPI can be arranged before money moves.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Manual 3.0i with very low verified miles, a single long-term owner and a stock appearance. Sport Package is claimed. Silver over black is a common colour combination.

Cooling system: expansion tank, radiator necks, water pump play and weep, hoses, thermostat operation
Oil filter housing gasket and valve cover leaks; VANOS rattle on cold start; DISA valve
Tire date codes; brake calipers and fluid after long low use
Rear trailing-arm bushings and the general rubber condition of the suspension
Clutch engagement and gearbox function; confirm a factory manual

what_would_change_verdict: A clean independent PPI with lift photos of a rust-free subframe, trunk floor and underbody would raise condition and documentation.
Paper service records or dealer reconditioning invoices (cooling, fluids, tires) would raise documentation and lower expected catch-up.
A price negotiated toward the fair-value range would materially improve price_value.
Evidence of significant rust, subframe cracking or a leaking or overheating cooling system would move it down sharply.
evidence.mission_note: This is exactly the bridge spec Jason wants: a 2002 Z3 3.0i manual within the ceiling and easy to resell. His bridge mode allows time to insist on a PPI and a sharper price, because the Michigan history and undocumented age-related service are the open questions.
evidence.rationale: The bought Carfax firmly establishes identity: a 2002 Z3 3.0i with a clean title, no reported accident, one corporate-fleet owner from 2002 to 2026 in Waterford, MI, and a consistent odometer trail to 20,947 mi. The same report shows only two independent-shop oil changes (2015, 2019) and no reported entry for cooling, belts, fluids or tires over 24 years. That points to long, low-use storage, where age rather than mileage drives the catch-up work. The car was bought at a fleet/lease auction in 08/2026 and titled to the dealer in 10/2026 after an unexplained Montana exempt record, with no reconditioning documented. Photos show a straight, clean, stock-looking roadster with a tidy top, but nothing from underneath, which matters after 24 Michigan winters. The $20,000 ask sits above the mileage-adjusted fair value of $13,840-$17,462. The '19+ wheels' and Sport Package entries appear to be data-feed claims, and the wheels look factory.
